report.summary: Reviewed chunk 3 of publish.py: egress gate, gh failure classifier, load_for_publish, publish_to_pr, read_pr_thread, _parse_comment. Claims checked and enumerated.
risks: screen_egress | medium | _EGRESS_HINT used but not defined in chunk; may be missing or defined elsewhere | check definition of _EGRESS_HINT in file

load_for_publish | high | Derives 'vendors_answered' by filtering requested that are in answered, then falling back to answered; may misrepresent when no vendor answered | verify logic against real transcript where some requested never answered
read_pr_thread | medium | _parse_comment function truncated; author parsing logic incomplete in chunk | review full _parse_comment implementation

_classify_failure | low | Order of checks: auth before not-found is correct per docstring, but rate-limit check before not-found may cause misclassification if rate limit message also contains 'not found' | ensure rate limit messages do not contain 'not found'

handoff.purpose: Implements egress gate, gh failure classification, load_for_publish, publish_to_pr, read_pr_thread, and _parse_comment.

symbols.name: screen_egress
symbols.note: Runs secret floor rule over evidence paths and channel texts; returns first hit or None.

symbols.name: _gh_argv
symbols.note: Prepends --repo argument to gh command if repo is provided.

symbols.name: _classify_failure
symbols.note: Maps gh invocation failure to (status, detail) based on stderr/stdout patterns.

symbols.name: _first_url
symbols.note: Extracts first http/https URL from text.

symbols.name: load_for_publish
symbols.note: Reconstructs verdict and turns from bus transcript file.

symbols.name: publish_to_pr
symbols.note: Renders deliberation, runs egress gate, optionally invokes gh to post PR comment.

symbols.name: read_pr_thread
symbols.note: Reads PR comments via gh and returns structured turns.

symbols.name: _parse_comment
symbols.note: Parses a gh comment object into PRTurn; tolerant of two author shapes.

claims.text: Returns ``(channel, rule)`` for the FIRST hit, or None if clean.
claims.why: Function iterates paths then channels, returns on first hit, else None.

claims.text: The returned rule is a fixed label / path fragment from ``sensitivity`` -- never matched text, so a refusal can be logged and reported without re-leaking the secret it refused
claims.why: secret_floor_rule behavior and return value not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Auth is tested before not-found because GitHub answers 404 -- not 403 -- for a private repo you are not authenticated to see; classifying that as ``pr_not_found`` would send an operator hunting for a PR that exists and is merely invisible to a logged-out CLI.
claims.why: Code checks auth patterns (not logged in, 401, etc.) before not-found patterns (404, no pull request, etc.).

claims.text: ``(verdict, turns)`` reconstructed from a stored bus transcript.
claims.why: Function loads transcript via bus.load_transcript, builds verdict dict and returns (verdict, turns).

claims.text: This function is the missing seam.
claims.why: Cannot verify historical context from this chunk.

claims.text: Only what the bus actually recorded.
claims.why: Verdict fields derived from transcript records; no outcome or convergence invented.

claims.text: Quorum comes from the roster records' ``participants``: a vendor is ANSWERED only if it actually produced a turn, not if it was merely seated.
claims.why: Code collects requested from roster records, answered from turn records with status 'spoke' only.

claims.text: Deriving it from the seat list would silently upgrade every short council to a full one.
claims.why: No seat list derivation in this chunk; claim about alternative approach.

claims.text: ``dry_run=True`` renders and gates but does NOT invoke the runner at all; the markdown comes back on the result.
claims.why: If dry_run, returns PublishResult with STATUS_DRY_RUN and markdown, no runner call.

claims.text: The gate still runs, so a dry run is an honest rehearsal rather than a way around the floor.
claims.why: screen_egress is called before dry_run check.

claims.text: The body goes to gh on STDIN via ``--body-file -``
claims.why: argv includes '--body-file', '-' not shown but implied by stdin payload; runner call passes body as stdin.

claims.text: a deliberation exceeds the Windows argv limit
claims.why: No evidence about Windows argv limits in this chunk.

claims.text: Never raises for an operational failure -- every outcome is a status in ``PUBLISH_STATUSES``.
claims.why: PUBLISH_STATUSES not defined in this chunk; function returns PublishResult in all branches, no explicit raises.

claims.text: Never raises for an operational failure; every outcome is a status in ``READ_STATUSES``.
claims.why: READ_STATUSES not defined in this chunk; function returns ThreadResult in all branches, no explicit raises.

claims.text: Nothing read here is authoritative: a reply is INPUT to a later round, not a verdict, and it is not on the hash-chained bus until the council appends it there.
claims.why: No comparison with bus or authority logic in this chunk.

claims.text: Tolerant of the two author shapes gh uses (``author.login`` from the GraphQL-backed ``pr view --json``, ``user.login`` from the REST-backed ``gh api``).
claims.why: Code truncated; cannot verify author extraction for both shapes.

observations.what: screen_egress uses _EGRESS_HINT constant which is not defined in this chunk; may be defined elsewhere in file.

load_for_publish derives 'vendors_answered' as [v for v in requested if v in answered] or answered; if no requested vendor answered, falls back to answered list which may be empty or contain unexpected entries.
_parse_comment is truncated; author parsing logic incomplete, potential silent failure if neither shape matches.
